newsitem.title: USA: Southern Q2 hurt by cool weather.
newsitem.headline: Southern Q2 hurt by cool weather.

text.p: Southern Co Thursday reported a drop in second quarter earnings to $0.31 from $0.43 a year ago, citing unusually cool weather.
The First Call consensus for the latest quarter was $0.40 per share.

"The unusually cool weather throughout our southeastern territory caused a decrease in demand responsible for the vast majority of the decline in earnings," Chief Executive Officer A.W. Dahlberg said.
Dahlberg said electricity use by retail customers in Southern Co's service area decreased 3.2 percent to 62.1 billion kilowatt-hours during the first half of 1997.

In-home electricity needs were down 12.3 percent to 17.0 billion kilowatt-hours. Electricity consumption by commercial customers -- offices, stores and other nonmanufacturing firms -- dropped 1.1 percent to 18.1 billion kilowatt-hours. Industrial energy use increased 2.1 percent to 26.5 billion kilowatt-hours.
Total sales of electricity to customers of Southern Co, including sales to other utilities, were down 3.1 percent to 71.8 billion kilowatt-hours for the first half of 1997.
